intro: Michigan runs its elections locally, through city and township clerks with help from county clerks.

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID if you have one. If you do not have a photo ID, you can still vote by signing an affidavit that says you do not have one.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register online or by mail
dates.detail: From Oct. 20 through Election Day you can still register, but only in person at your local clerk's office with proof of where you live. You have until 8 pm on Election Day.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Any registered voter can vote early in person for federal and statewide elections. Your local clerk sets the sites and hours, so check with your clerk.

src.label: Michigan Department of State, early in-person voting

dates.label: Absentee ballot application deadline, mail or online
dates.detail: Your local clerk must receive your application by 5 pm on the Friday before Election Day. Michigan does not require a reason to vote absentee.

src.label: Michigan Department of State, absentee voting

dates.label: In-person absentee application deadline
dates.detail: If you are registered at your current address, you can apply in person at your local clerk's office until 4 pm the day before Election Day.

src.label: Michigan Department of State, absentee voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm, local time. An absentee ballot must be received by your local clerk by 8 pm, or put in a drop box by 8 pm. A postmark is not enough.
